items.title: Complex-oriented diagonal Thom classes realize exceptional exchange on supports
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the analytic six-functor and equivariant constructible suppliers below. In the analytic constructible six-functor setting, let $M$ be the analytic space of a smooth complex algebraic variety of pure dimension $d$, and let $q:A\to M$, $u:B\to M$ be morphisms of complex algebraic varieties with fiber product $T=A\times_MB$; write $a:T\to A$ and $b:T\to B$ for the projections, so that $qa=ub$ and the square is Cartesian. Assume the supplied duality construction has localization, tensor–Hom adjunction, coherent exchange maps, and the smooth orientation normalized by the positive compactly supported generator on a complex coordinate ball ([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]], [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]), with its equivariant constructible form supplied by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. The refined pullback of dualizing classes on the support $A\times B$ by the ambient middle diagonal $M\to M\times M$ is the operation induced by the mate $\mathrm{ex}:a^*q^!\to b^!u^*$ of the base-change morphism $u^*q_!\to b_!a^*$ of this square, after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive middle-diagonal Thom class and lowers Borel–Moore degree by $2d$, even for singular, nontransverse supports. Ordered iterated diagonals are compatible with composed refined operations. For a complex vector bundle, zero-section self-intersection is cap product with its oriented Euler class.
items.strategy: Direct supported purity counit, proper pullback, exceptional adjunction, graph factorization and coherent counit composition; ordered normal Thom products and rank-c zero-section Euler restriction. AC inherited as declared in current item.

items.title: Equivariant Borel–Moore homology and oriented correspondence convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the equivariant
constructible and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Let $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}_{n_v}(\mathbb C)$,
let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, and use bounded algebraically constructible complexes of
$k$-sheaves in the analytic topology, in the equivariant derived category
$D^b_{G,c}(-;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]].
All functors are derived.

**Dualizing normalization and Borel–Moore homology.** The equivariant dualizing object is
normalized by $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$, rather than by the dimension of the quotient stack; here
$\omega_X=a_X^!k$ is the ordinary constructible dualizing object and
$\omega_X^G\simeq k_X[2d]$ for a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$
([[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]). Define
$$H_j^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;k)=H_G^{-j}(X,\omega_X^G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(X;k)}(k_X,\omega_X^G[-j]).$$
Equivalently, use the general linear Stiefel approximations $U$ and their geometric quotients
supplied by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
with $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$. In each fixed degree, once the supplied
bounded-Hom comparison applies, the group is the stable value
$H_{j+2b}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;k)$. Comparison on products of sufficiently acyclic
resolutions makes it independent of the chosen such stage. Other free smooth models require
the same bounded-Hom and quotient hypotheses; freeness alone does not assert stabilization. Ordinary
Borel–Moore homology is the case $G=1$ in the same formula, i.e.
$H_j^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;k)=\operatorname{Hom}(k_X,\omega_X[-j])$, and the smooth complex orientation
gives $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$ for $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d$.

**Correspondences.** Let $f_i:X_i\to E$ be finitely many proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps
with $X_i$ smooth of pure complex dimension $d_i$. Put $Z_{ij}=X_i\times_EX_j$ (reduced
analytically), $T_{ijk}=X_i\times_EX_j\times_EX_k$, and let $h:T_{ijk}\to Z_{ik}$ forget the
middle point; it is proper, being the base change of $f_j$
([[lem-proper-stable-base-change]]). The first coordinate is the source.
For $a\in H_p^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij})$, $b\in H_q^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{jk})$, define
$$a*b=h_*\Delta_{X_j}^{!}(a\boxtimes b)\in H_{p+q-2d_j}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ik}).$$
Here $\Delta_{X_j}^{!}$ is the refined oriented middle-diagonal operation on supports of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]]: it
restricts the external class to $T_{ijk}$ by the Thom class of the complex normal bundle $TX_j$
of $X_j\hookrightarrow X_j\times X_j$. It is defined on arbitrary closed supports; no
transversality of $Z_{ij}$ and $Z_{jk}$ is assumed. Proper pushforward is the dualizing trace.
The ordered coordinates are $(i,j,j,k)$, and the two middle factors are contracted without a
permutation. If intermediate indices differ, the product is set to zero. Put degree $d_i+d_j-p$
on the $(i,j)$ corner. The normalized diagonal class $[\Delta_{X_i}]$ has corner degree zero.

**Sheaf model.** The sheaf model of the refined Thom operation uses the exchange morphism
$v'^*u^!\to u'^!v^*$ for the middle Cartesian square: with $u:Z_{ij}\to X_j$,
$v:Z_{jk}\to X_j$, $T=Z_{ij}\times_{X_j}Z_{jk}$ and projections $v':T\to Z_{ij}$,
$u':T\to Z_{jk}$, the morphism is obtained as the adjunction mate of proper base change
$v^*u_!\xrightarrow{\sim}u'_!v'^*$. Explicitly, its value at $C$ is adjoint to
$u'_!v'^*u^!C\to v^*u_!u^!C\to v^*C$, the first map being inverse base change and the
second the exceptional counit. It is a morphism, not an asserted isomorphism for arbitrary supports.
Its orientation is fixed by the Thom class restricting to $+1$ on every positively
complex-oriented normal fiber. Agreement of this model with the stated refined geometric
operation, and compatibility with composition, are proved in
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]] after the
foundational six-functor inputs are available.

**Well-formedness.** The definition is independent of the chosen sufficiently acyclic Stiefel stage
because the stable Borel value exists and the product-resolution comparisons are coherent by
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]; the product is
defined because the refined middle-diagonal operation of
[[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] is
defined on arbitrary closed supports and $h$ is proper, so its dualizing trace is available; the
degree bookkeeping is fixed by the pure complex dimension $d_j$ of the middle factor. The claim
that the sheaf model and the geometric operation agree, and that the product is compatible with
composition and units, is not assumed here: it is the content of
[[thm-verdier-duality-identification-intertwines-yoneda-product-and-convolution]], which is
recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that theorem depends on this
definition. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the cited suppliers, including proper
base-change stability; their descent, injective, Thom and Borel constructions declare it;
the definition itself introduces no further choice principle.
items.strategy: Read the complete current Definition and all six suppliers, including actual simplicial, Stiefel-bound, proper-base-change and normalized-equivariant-duality arguments. The mate v-prime-star u-shriek -> u-prime-shriek v-star is typed from the X_j category to T; its left adjoint is inverse base change followed by the exceptional counit. It is not asserted invertible. For fixed j the Hom comparison applies eventually to k_X and omega_X[-j]; omega on X_N is shifted by -2b, hence ordinary BM degree j+2b. Only sufficiently acyclic Stiefel stages/common product comparisons are claimed. Middle forgetting is the base change of proper f_j; corner degree d_i+d_j-p and drop 2d_j are additive. Empty family/support gives zero, G=1 is the identity model, and zero dimension gives no drop. AC inherited. Archived ill-typed exchange and freeness-only approximation claim are fully repaired. Direct references outside batch 40 (quiver incidence Definition, signed KLR Ext theorem and geometric PBW theorem) retain source-first order and summed shifts; no correction is required by this Definition change. Independent downstream PBW/calculus defects reported by the reader remain routed for batch 43/Step 3b, not repaired here. Owned direct consumers will be reviewed in the generated order.

items.title: Proper-pushforward Ext is equivariant Borel–Moore homology of the fiber product
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible
six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. Use the constructible equivariant setting
$D^b_{G,c}(E;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]
and proper $G$-equivariant algebraic maps $f_i:X_i\to E$ with smooth sources $X_i$ of pure complex
dimension $d_i$, as in [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]].
Put $L_i=f_{i!}k_{X_i}[d_i]$. For every integer $r$ and every pair $(i,j)$ there is a natural
isomorphism
$$\Phi_{ij}^r:\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{G,c}(E;k)}(L_i,L_j[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k).$$
All groups are degreewise finite-dimensional for these finite-type algebraic varieties and $G$;
no finite-dimensionality of their direct sum over all degrees is asserted. The isomorphism is
equivariant-cohomology linear, commutes with enlargement of the Borel approximation, and is
natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before smooth orientation is applied. No
semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity, or smoothness of $E$ or $Z_{ij}$ is required.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The adjunction chain. Write $p:Z_{ij}\to X_i$ and $q:Z_{ij}\to X_j$ for the projections and put $t=r+d_j-d_i$. Removing the source shift by $[-d_i]$ and using the adjunction $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ of [F1] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_E(f_{i!}k_i,f_{j!}k_j[t])=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(k_i,f_i^!f_{j!}k_j[t])$. In the Cartesian square with lower arrow $f_j$ and right arrow $f_i$, the extraordinary proper base change of [F1] gives $f_i^!f_{j!}k_j=p_*q^!k_j$, because both maps are proper and the square is Cartesian; the adjunction $p^*\dashv p_*$ then identifies the group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{Z_{ij}}(k_Z,q^!k_j[t])$. This is the complete cornerwise chain and it is valid for every integer $r$, including negative $r$. [F1, given]

2.1 Orientation and the degree. The smooth orientation of [F1] on the smooth pure $d_j$-dimensional source $X_j$ says $k_{X_j}=\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]$, and dualizing transitivity for $q$ gives $q^!k_{X_j}=q^!\omega_{X_j}[-2d_j]=\omega_{Z_{ij}}[-2d_j]$. Substituting $t=r+d_j-d_i$, the group of step 1.1 is $\operatorname{Hom}(k_Z,\omega_Z[r-d_i-d_j])$, which is exactly $H_{d_i+d_j-r}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(Z_{ij};k)$ in the normalization of [F3]. At a finite free smooth approximation of dimension offset $b=\dim_{\mathbb C}U-\dim_{\mathbb C}G$, the space $X_j\times_GU$ is smooth of complex dimension $d_j+b$ while the descended complex retains the shift $d_j$, so the identical calculation gives ordinary Borel–Moore degree $d_i+d_j+2b-r$; removing $2b$ gives the stated equivariant degree, and no stack-dimension shift is inserted into $\omega_X^G$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Naturality, linearity and finiteness. Every map in the chain of steps 1.1 and 2.1 is an adjunction, base-change or orientation map supplied naturally by [F1], so the composite is natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before the smooth orientation is applied and is compatible with composition of the $f_i$. By [F2] these maps commute with the approximation transition pullbacks on the bounded ranges, so the composite induces an isomorphism in each stable degree; coherent scalar pullback from the base point together with the projection formula of [F1] gives equivariant-cohomology linearity. Degreewise finiteness is exactly the conclusion of [F4] for bounded algebraically constructible objects, and it is asserted nowhere that the direct sum over all degrees is finite-dimensional. Smoothness of the sources is used only for the orientation in step 2.1, and properness only in the base change and in the identification $f_{i!}=f_{i*}$; no semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity or smoothness of $E$ or of the fiber products $Z_{ij}$ is used. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Verdier-duality identification intertwines Yoneda product and oriented convolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the constructible
six-functor and Borel-stabilization suppliers. For the data and cornerwise maps $\Phi$ of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]], let
$\alpha:L_i\to L_j[r]$ and $\beta:L_j\to L_k[s]$. With multiplication
$\alpha*\beta=\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ one has
$$\Phi_{ik}^{r+s}(\beta[r]\circ\alpha)=\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)*\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta).$$
Here the right product is the external-product, refined middle-diagonal Thom intersection,
proper-pushforward convolution of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]],
not a product transported by definition from Ext. The map sends $\operatorname{id}_{L_i}$ to
$[\Delta_{X_i}]$. Consequently the direct sum of all corners is an isomorphism of unital graded
algebras with this opposite-composition convention; nonmatching corners multiply to zero.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Typed correspondences. Put $t=r+d_j-d_i$ and $w=s+d_k-d_j$. Under the chain of [F3] the maps $\alpha$ and $\beta$ correspond to kernel forms $\kappa:k_A\to q^!k_j[t]$ and $\lambda:k_B\to v^!k_k[w]$, equivalently to cohomological correspondences $U:q_!k_A\to k_j[t]$ and $V:v_!k_B\to k_k[w]$; here $k_j=k_{X_j}$ and $k_k=k_{X_k}$. The middle square $(a,b;q,u)$ is Cartesian with $qa=ub$, and the three-factor identities $pa=\ell h$, $vb=mh$ hold by construction of the triple fiber product. [given, F3]

2.1 The explicit composite. Let $\mathrm{BC}:b_!a^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*q_!$ be the proper base change isomorphism of [F4]. Form the map $$W:(vb)_!k_T=v_!b_!a^*k_A\xrightarrow{v_!\mathrm{BC}}v_!u^*q_!k_A\xrightarrow{v_!u^*U}v_!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{V[t]}k_k[t+w].$$ Its adjoint $k_T\to(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$ under $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$ is the composite $k_T\xrightarrow{a^*\kappa}a^*q^!k_j[t]\to b^!u^*k_j[t]=b^!k_B[t]\xrightarrow{b^!\lambda[t]}(vb)^!k_k[t+w]$, in which the middle arrow is the mate exchange of $\mathrm{BC}$. The equality follows by applying the adjunction $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$ to both maps: the defining evaluation of the mate reproduces exactly the three arrows of $W$, so no exchange isomorphism beyond $\mathrm{BC}$ is assumed. [F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Geometric interpretation of the mate. Put $S=A\times B$, $F=(q,u):S\to X_j\times X_j$, and $\theta:T\hookrightarrow S$. By [F1] the pulled-back positive purity counit is $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d_j]\to k_S$. The external dualizing class corresponding to $\kappa\boxtimes\lambda$ has degree $n+n'$, where $n=d_i+d_j-r$ and $n'=d_j+d_k-s$ by [F3]; composing it with $g_F$ and taking the adjoint under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ gives a class of degree $n+n'-2d_j$ on $T$. The graph-factorization and composition-of-counits comparison proved in [F1] identifies this supported cap map with the mate in step 2.1, followed by $b^!\lambda[t]$. Thus its representative is exactly the adjoint of $W$. The purity counit, its pullback, and the mate are fixed global morphisms; the positive normal-ball generator fixes their orientation, while their equality on arbitrary supports follows from that supported adjunction comparison. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 Pushing the correspondence to the third corner. Its adjoint representative is $U_C:m_!k_C\xrightarrow{m_!\eta_h}m_!h_*k_T=(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{W}k_k[t+w]$, where $\eta_h:k_C\to h_*h^*k_C=h_*k_T$ is the ordinary adjunction unit and $h_*=h_!$ by [F4]. In kernel form this is $k_C\to h_*k_T\to h_*h^!m^!k_k[t+w]\xrightarrow{\epsilon_h}m^!k_k[t+w]$ with $\epsilon_h$ the dualizing proper trace, and dualizing transitivity identifies the middle dualizing object with $\omega_T[-2d_k+t+w]$. Step 3.1 therefore identifies the class on $C$ represented by $U_C$ with $h_*\Delta_{X_j}^!(\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)\boxtimes\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta))$, which by [F2] is the convolution product $\Phi_{ij}^r(\alpha)*\Phi_{jk}^s(\beta)$. [F2, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 The composition square commutes. The inverse of the chain of [F3] sends $U$ to $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_p}f_{i!}p_*k_A=f_{j!}q_!k_A\xrightarrow{f_{j!}U}f_{j!}k_j[t]$ and $V$ to the analogous map built from $u,v$, where $\eta_p:k_i\to p_*p^*k_i=p_*k_A$ is the adjunction unit and $f_{j!}=f_{j*}$. In the composite of these two maps, naturality of $\eta_u:\operatorname{id}\to u_*u^*$ moves $f_{j!}U$ past the second unit, and proper base change $u^*q_!\cong b_!a^*$ identifies the resulting two units with the unit $\eta_{pa}:k_i\to(pa)_*k_T$; the Beck–Chevalley unit identity is the transpose of the triangle equations under $f_{i!}\dashv f_i^!$ and $(vb)_!\dashv(vb)^!$, so both routes give the same morphism $f_{i!}k_i\xrightarrow{f_{i!}\eta_{pa}}f_{k!}(vb)_!k_T\xrightarrow{f_{k!}W}f_{k!}k_k[t+w]$. Applying the inverse map to $U_C$ gives the same expression, because $pa=\ell h$ and the composed-unit formula $\eta_{\ell h}=\ell_*\eta_h\ell^*\circ\eta_\ell$ follows from the same triangle equations. Hence the product square commutes for arbitrary cohomological correspondences, before orientation or grading is applied; this is the compatibility of products asserted in the Statement. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Shifts, degrees and signs. Restore the object shifts: $t+w=r+s+d_k-d_i$. The corner degrees $d_i+d_j-r$ and $d_j+d_k-s$ add and lose $2d_j$ under the refined intersection, giving $d_i+d_k-r-s$, which is the corner degree of the output. At a finite approximation the middle factor has dimension $d_j+b$ and each incoming ordinary Borel–Moore degree acquires $2b$, so the output acquires exactly $2b$ and the stable equivariant degree is unchanged. Homogeneous maps compose as $V[t]\circ U$, hence as $\beta[r]\circ\alpha$ after restoring shifts, with no interchanged factors and no additional sign; the only possible sign in re-ordering the complex normal factors is $(-1)^{(2d_j)(2d_j)}=+1$, and external products follow the usual tensor Koszul convention with no permutation occurring here. [F1, F2, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 Units and the algebra statement. Let $\delta:X_i\to Z_{ii}$ be the diagonal, with $p\delta=q\delta=\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$. The cohomological correspondence for its fundamental class is $U_\delta:q_!k_{Z_{ii}}\to q_!\delta_*k_{X_i}=k_{X_i}$, induced by restriction $k_{Z_{ii}}\to\delta_*k_{X_i}$. Its inverse image under the chain [F3] is $f_{i!}k_{X_i}\to f_{i!}p_*k_{Z_{ii}}\to f_{i!}k_{X_i}$; restriction of the first unit to $\delta$ is the identity, so this composite is the identity. The adjoint kernel of $U_\delta$ is the proper trace of the positive fundamental class of $X_i$, since $\delta^!q^!k_{X_i}=k_{X_i}$. Hence $\Phi_{ii}^0(\operatorname{id}_{L_i})=\delta_*[X_i]=[\Delta_{X_i}]$, of corner degree zero. Step 5.1 transfers associativity and these units from shifted composition; the unit on the finite sum is $\sum_i[\Delta_{X_i}]$. The cornerwise bijections of [F3] therefore give the claimed unital graded algebra isomorphism, with nonmatching corners zero by [F2]. AC is inherited through [A1]. [A1, F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: Stable-flag incidence spaces admit the oriented proper correspondence calculus
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited through the smooth-projective
flag-variety and Euler-to-Chern suppliers. Let $Q$ be any finite loopless quiver, allowing
multiple arrows and arrows in both directions, let $V= igoplus_vV_v$ be finite-dimensional over
$\mathbb C$, and put $G=\prod_v\mathrm{GL}(V_v)$ and
$E_V= igoplus_{h:v	o w}\operatorname{Hom}(V_v,V_w)$. For a word $
u$ of vertex labels with
multiplicities $\dim V_v$, let $B_
u$ be its graded complete flag variety and
$X_
u=\{(x,F)\in E_V	imes B_
u:x_h(F^a_v)\subseteq F^a_w	ext{ for all }a,h\}$. Then
$X_
u	o B_
u$ is a complex algebraic vector bundle, $X_
u$ is smooth, and
$\pi_
u:X_
u	o E_V$ is projective. Every middle-forgetting projection
$X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_\eta	imes_{E_V}X_	heta	o X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_	heta$ is proper. All
orientations and refined middle-diagonal operations required by the preceding Ext/convolution
theorems exist equivariantly, without a smoothness or transversality assertion for fiber products.
With $d_
u=\dim_{\mathbb C}X_
u$ and $L_
u=R\pi_{
u!}k[d_
u]$, those theorems apply in every
corner. Smooth vector-bundle projections and flag-bundle projections have their complex-oriented
pullbacks, and zero-section self-intersection is cap product with the top Chern class of the
bundle.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Incidence as an associated bundle. A zero-dimensional $V_v$ has the unique empty flag, so its flag variety and group factor are points. Fix a graded reference flag. Its stabilizer $P_
u=\prod_vP_v$ is the product of the upper triangular subgroups of the individual $\mathrm{GL}(V_v)$, and by the transitive action of [F3] its orbit is $B_
u=\prod_v\operatorname{Flag}(V_v)$, a product of smooth projective flag varieties, so $B_
u=G/P_
u$ is smooth projective. On an ordinary flag chart choose ordered basis vectors compatible with the flags; the stability condition $x_h(F^a_v)\subseteq F^a_w$ for an arrow $h:v	o w$ says that the matrix coefficient of $x_h$ from source position $a$ to target position $b$ vanishes whenever $b>a$, positions being read in the full word $
u$. Over the chart the fiber of $X_
u	o B_
u$ is therefore the fixed linear subspace $S_
u\subset E_V$ of tuples whose entries vanish in the forbidden positions, of dimension the sum over arrows of the number of allowed pairs; the stabilizer $P_
u$ preserves $S_
u$ and the chart trivializations identify $X_
u=G	imes_{P_
u}S_
u$ as a complex algebraic vector bundle over $B_
u=G/P_
u$. Multiple arrows contribute separate summands, and arrows in both directions impose conditions on separate matrices. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Smoothness, projectivity and properness. By step 1.1 the total space $X_
u$ is the total space of a vector bundle over the smooth variety $B_
u$, hence is smooth of pure complex dimension $d_
u=\sum_v\dim\operatorname{Flag}(V_v)+\dim S_
u$. The incidence conditions are polynomial in the chart coordinates, so $X_
u$ is closed in $E_V	imes B_
u$, and $\pi_
u$ is the composite of this closed immersion with the product projection. Since $B_
u$ is a closed subvariety of a product of projective spaces by [F3], the product projection $E_V	imes B_
u	o E_V$ is a closed subvariety of a trivial projective-space bundle over the affine space $E_V$, so it is projective, and passing to the closed subvariety $X_
u$ keeps it projective; by [F5] a projective morphism over the affine base is proper. The middle-forgetting map $X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_\eta	imes_{E_V}X_	heta	o X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_	heta$ is the base change of $\pi_\eta$ along the projection $X_
u	imes_{E_V}X_	heta	o E_V$, hence proper by the base-change stability in [F5], although neither its fibers nor its total space is asserted smooth. [F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Orientations and equivariance. Each $X_
u$ is smooth by step 2.1, with its complex orientation and diagonal normal bundle $TX_
u$. The supported Thom operation of [F1] therefore gives the refined middle-diagonal operation on all fiber products, and step 2.1 supplies the proper traces. These are $G$-equivariant constructions, descending to the Stiefel models with the stabilization comparisons of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]]. Thus [F2] applies with shift $d_
u$. On a Stiefel quotient the graded flags are nested subspaces of the fixed frame spaces, hence a closed incidence locus in a product of Grassmannians, projective by the same incidence equations and projective-product construction as step 2.1. The incidence approximation is the associated vector bundle of step 1.1 over that projective base. Fiber scaling retracts its total to the zero section, so [F3] applied to the projective base gives CW type for the total. The base has a metric from its finite-polyhedral model. A finite trivializing cover of the compact base admits a partition of unity supported inside its charts; multiplying the local vector coordinates by these functions embeds the total bundle into the product of the base with a finite-dimensional vector space, giving the total a metric as well. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Zero sections and relative orientations. The complex bundles on the metric approximations of step 3.1 have finite trivializing covers. For a finite trivializing cover $(U_i)$ of a metric space $X$, put $r_i(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,X\setminus U_i)$, using $r_i=1$ when $U_i=X$, and $R(x)=\max_i r_i(x)>0$. The continuous functions $\psi_i=\max(0,r_i-R/2)$ have positive sum and support contained in $\{r_i\ge R/2\}\subset U_i$; normalizing their sum gives a subordinate finite numeration. Hence the Thom/Euler clause of [F1] applies. Zero-section self-intersection is cap product with the Euler class. Pulling back along a CW-model homotopy equivalence and using naturality identifies it with the top Chern class by [F4], componentwise; extend the integral identity to $k$. A smooth vector-bundle or flag-bundle projection of relative complex dimension $r$ locally has the product duality formula $f^!=f^*[2r]$. Complex transition maps preserve the fiber orientation, so these formulas glue and give the oriented Borel–Moore pullback of degree $2r$. Projection formula and the trace/base-change mates of [F1] give compatibility with proper pushforward and refined Cartesian pullback, without asserting ordinary purity on singular fiber products. These are the calculus operations, rather than numerical crossing formulas. AC is inherited through [A1]. [A1, F1, F4, step 3.1] ∎

title: Equivariant Borel Moore Correspondence Convolution And Constructible Ext Examples

items.title: Unequal-dimensional proper pushforwards carry the summed-dimension Ext/Borel–Moore degree
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. For
the trivial group $G$, $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$ and $X_2=\mathbb P^1$ with $d_1=0$,
$d_2=1$, put $L_1=k$ and $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. Then
$\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)$ is $k$ for $r=-1,1$ and zero otherwise, and the corresponding
summed-dimension Borel–Moore degrees $d_1+d_2-r$ are $2$ and $0$; the reverse corner
$\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_2,L_1)$ has the same two nonzero degrees. The unaugmented shifts
$2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_1-r=-r$ and $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_2-r=2-r$ give the wrong degrees in at least
one corner, so the summed $d_1+d_2$ normalization of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] is the one
compatible with the two unequal source dimensions.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The two sources and the objects. The map $f_1:\mathrm{pt}\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper with $d_1=0$ and $L_1=f_{1!}k_{\mathrm{pt}}[0]=k$, and the map $f_2:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$ is proper with $d_2=1$ and $L_2=f_{2!}k_{\mathbb P^1}[1]=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$, the last equality using $f_{2*}=f_{2!}$ for proper $f_2$. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathrm{pt}\times_{\mathrm{pt}}\mathbb P^1=\mathbb P^1$. [F2, F3, given]

1.2 The cohomology of the projective line. By [F3] the Schubert cells give $\mathbb P^1$ one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell, so its constant-coefficient cellular cochain complex is $k\oplus k[-2]$. By [F4] it computes singular cohomology, and [F5] identifies this with constant-sheaf cohomology: $H^0=H^2=k$ and the other groups vanish. A complex of vector spaces with these cohomology groups is quasi-isomorphic to $k\oplus k[-2]$: choose cocycles representing the two generators to obtain a cochain map from $k\oplus k[-2]$ to the complex inducing these cohomology isomorphisms. Thus $R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)\simeq k\oplus k[-2]$. [F3, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 The forward corner. For complexes of $k$-vector spaces one has $\operatorname{Hom}(k,C[n])=H^n(C)$, so $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)=\operatorname{Hom}(k,R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1+r])=H^{1+r}(\mathbb P^1,k)$, which by step 1.2 is $k$ for $r=-1$ and for $r=1$ and is zero otherwise; in particular both nonzero groups are one-dimensional. [step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The reverse corner. Similarly $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_2,L_1)=\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1],k[r])=\operatorname{Hom}(R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k),k[r-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(k\oplus k[-2],k[r-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(k,k[r-1])\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(k,k[r+1])$, which is $k$ exactly when $r=1$ or $r=-1$ and is zero otherwise; so both corners have the same two nonzero degrees. [step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The degree check. By [F1] the isomorphism $\Phi^r_{12}$ identifies $\operatorname{Ext}^r(L_1,L_2)$ with $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{d_1+d_2-r}(\mathbb P^1;k)=H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{1-r}(\mathbb P^1;k)$: the degree $r=-1$ corresponds to Borel–Moore degree $2$ and $r=1$ to Borel–Moore degree $0$, and the reverse corner $(2,1)$ gives the same two degrees. These values match the computation: by [F2] and step 1.2, $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_j(\mathbb P^1;k)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D_c^b(\mathbb P^1;k)}(k_{\mathbb P^1},k_{\mathbb P^1}[2-j])=H^{2-j}(\mathbb P^1;k)$ is $k$ for $j=2$ and for $j=0$. The single-source shifts fail this comparison in both corners: $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_1-r=-r$ is $1$ for $r=-1$ and $-1$ for $r=1$, and $2\dim_{\mathbb C}X_2-r=2-r$ is $3$ for $r=-1$ and $1$ for $r=1$, while the required degrees are $2$ and $0$. Hence the summed $d_1+d_2$ normalization is the one compatible with the two unequal source dimensions. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.2, step 3.1] ∎

items.title: A point and projective-line check of source-first convolution and opposite composition
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited constructible and cellular suppliers. In
the point/projective-line geometry with $E=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_1=\mathrm{pt}$, $X_2=\mathbb P^1$,
$d_1=0$, $d_2=1$ and $L_1=k$, $L_2=R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]$ in the setting of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], let
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)$ be the unit $k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ and let
$\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^{1}(L_2,L_1)$ be point evaluation
$R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)[1]\to k[1]$, that is, evaluation $H^0(\mathbb P^1,k)\to k$ shifted by
$1$ and extended by zero on $H^2$. Then
$\alpha*\beta=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention of
[[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]], and under the
correspondence isomorphism of
[[thm-proper-pushforward-ext-is-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-of-the-fiber-product]] one has
$[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$: the refined diagonal intersection of the fundamental
class of $\mathbb P^1$ with the point class is the point class, and proper pushforward to the
point corner gives its generator.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The geometry and the cohomology of the projective line. The fiber products are $Z_{12}=Z_{21}=\mathbb P^1$. By [F3] its Schubert CW structure has one $0$-cell and one $2$-cell, so the cellular cochain complex is $k\oplus k[-2]$. By [F4] it computes singular cohomology, and [F6] identifies this with constant-sheaf cohomology. Choosing cocycles representing the two generators gives a quasi-isomorphism $k\oplus k[-2]\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$. Hence $L_2\simeq k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ and $L_1=k$. [F3, F4, F6, algebra]

2.1 The two classes and their composites. The unit $\alpha:k\to R\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,k)$ includes the degree-zero summand, generating $\operatorname{Ext}^{-1}(L_1,L_2)=k$. Evaluation at a point projects to that summand; its shift $\beta:L_2\to k[1]$ generates $\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_2,L_1)=k$, since $\operatorname{Hom}(k[-2],k)=0$. Therefore $\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$. The reverse composite $\alpha[1]\circ\beta$ is also nonzero: it is the projector of $L_2=k[1]\oplus k[-1]$ onto $k[1]$, and is neither zero nor $\operatorname{id}_{L_2}$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The convolution check. Apply [F2] with $(i,j,k)=(1,2,1)$ and degrees $r=-1$, $s=1$ to the composable pair $\alpha:L_1\to L_2[r]$ and $\beta:L_2\to L_1[s]$: since $\beta[r]\circ\alpha=\beta[-1]\circ\alpha=\operatorname{id}_k$ by step 2.1, the product theorem gives $\Phi_{11}^{0}(\operatorname{id}_k)=\Phi_{12}^{-1}(\alpha)*\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)$, so $\alpha*\beta=\operatorname{id}_k$ in the source-first convention, and the right-hand side is the convolution product of [F1]. The corner degrees are $d_1+d_2-r=2$ for $\alpha$ and $d_2+d_1-s=0$ for $\beta$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 The geometric product. The adjunction chain of [F1] sends $\alpha$ to $\operatorname{id}_{k_{\mathbb P^1}}$, hence to the positive fundamental class $[\mathbb P^1]$. Write $i:\mathrm{pt}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^1$ for the evaluation point. Evaluation is the global-sections image of $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k$, and its adjoint under $R\Gamma\dashv a^!$, $a:\mathbb P^1\to\mathrm{pt}$, is the composite $k_{\mathbb P^1}\to i_*k=i_*i^!\omega_{\mathbb P^1}\to\omega_{\mathbb P^1}$, with the last arrow the proper trace. Thus $\Phi_{21}^{1}(\beta)=i_*[\mathrm{pt}]$ with coefficient $+1$. Geometrically $\mathbb P^1\times\{i\}$ meets the middle diagonal of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ transversely at $(i,i)$; the map from its tangent line to the complex normal line of the diagonal is an isomorphism, preserving the real orientation. The positive Thom cap of [F5] therefore gives that point with multiplicity $+1$, and proper pushforward to $Z_{11}=\mathrm{pt}$ gives $[\mathrm{pt}]$. This computes $[\mathbb P^1]*[\mathrm{pt}]=[\mathrm{pt}]$, with middle degree drop $2$ and no permutation sign, agreeing with step 3.1. It verifies a transverse instance of the calculus, not its general nontransverse case. AC is inherited through [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
